functions.name: core_clock_init
functions.brief: Bring up the clock tree for the project's `clock` level (oscillator, PLL, flash wait states, bus prescalers) and start SysTick. Generated per project by coregen into core_init.c and called by core_init(); call it again only to restore the clocks by hand (core_stop_for already does after a wake).

functions.name: core_sleep
functions.brief: Sleep until any interrupt (CPU stopped, peripherals running).

functions.name: core_stop_for
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode for a number of seconds, then wake and restore clocks. Uses the RTC wakeup timer (LSI). Returns after wake with PLL + SysTick restored; core_millis() advances by the time slept, as the RTC measured it. If the watchdog is running, sleeps in chunks of half its timeout and feeds it in between. Core.ST.L4 with a USB host awake on the bus: waits in Sleep mode so the host can still reach it (see the USB note at the top).

params.name: seconds
params.description: Seconds to spend in Stop mode.

functions.name: core_stop_until_on_change_timeout
functions.signature: core_stop_until_on_change_timeout(uint8_t pad, uint32_t edge, uint32_t timeout_ms)
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode until a GPIO edge on the given pad, or until `timeout_ms` has passed (0 = no timeout). Configures the pad as input, arms its EXTI, enters Stop, and restores clocks on wake. If the watchdog is running, wakes every half timeout to feed it and goes back to sleep. Core.ST.L4 with a USB host awake on the bus: waits in Sleep mode (see the USB note at the top). Already at the wake level: EXTI latches only edges that happen after it is armed, so a line that is already at its wake level — a sensor INT held low until serviced, for EDGE_FALLING — would never wake the Core. After arming, this reads the pad and returns 1 at once if it is already low (EDGE_FALLING) or high (EDGE_RISING). EDGE_BOTH always waits for a change.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Longest time to stay asleep, measured on the RTC; 0 waits for the edge however long it takes.

functions.return_desc: 1 = woken by the pad (or it was already at the wake level), 0 = timed out, -1 = the pad can't take an edge interrupt.

functions.name: core_stop_until_on_change
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode until a GPIO edge occurs on the given pad (no timeout). Returns right away if the pad can't take an edge interrupt, or if it is already at the level the edge wakes on (see core_stop_until_on_change_timeout()). If the watchdog is running, wakes every half timeout to feed it and goes back to sleep.

functions.name: core_standby_for
functions.brief: Enter Standby mode with RTC wakeup after the given seconds. On success it does not return — the MCU resets on wake. Check core_woke_from_standby() at the top of main() to detect a Standby wake. Watchdog: the IWDG keeps counting through Standby and nothing feeds it until main() runs again, and Standby can't be split into fed chunks. So while the watchdog is running this refuses — returns CORE_ERROR without sleeping — unless seconds is at most half the watchdog timeout (2 s with the default 5 s watchdog). Use core_stop_for() for longer sleeps. (Core.ST.H5: no check.)
functions.return_desc: CORE_ERROR if refused because of the watchdog; does not return otherwise.

functions.name: core_standby_until_on_change
functions.brief: Enter Standby mode until a GPIO edge on the given pad (via WKUP pin). Does not return — MCU resets on wake. Not all pads support WKUP; returns without entering Standby if the pad has no WKUP capability, or if the watchdog is running (it would reset the Core long before most edges). On Core.ST.L4.2: pad 8 (PA0 = WKUP1) and pad 7 (PA2 = WKUP4).

functions.name: core_stop
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode (caller manages wakeup source + clock recovery). A running watchdog keeps counting and is not fed: wake within its timeout. On the WBA the caller also owns the Stop 1 wait-state/HDIV5 rules (RM0493 §11.7.7).

functions.name: core_standby
functions.brief: Enter Standby (caller manages wakeup source). Does not return. A running watchdog keeps counting through Standby and resets the Core at its timeout.

functions.name: core_woke_from_standby
functions.brief: Returns 1 if the MCU woke from Standby. The flag survives later resets until core_clear_standby_flag() — call that once you've handled the wake.

functions.name: core_clear_standby_flag
functions.brief: Clear the Standby wake flag. Call after core_woke_from_standby() returns 1.

functions.name: core_watchdog_start_seconds
functions.brief: Start the independent watchdog with a timeout in seconds (convenience). For finer control use core_watchdog_start() from core_watchdog.h which accepts milliseconds.

functions.name: core_reset
functions.brief: Reset the Core. Does not return. With a BLE central connected (Core.ST.W5), the link is dropped first so the central sees a clean disconnect (waits at most 200 ms). Pending USB serial output is flushed (Core.ST.L4 / H5: waits at most 50 ms for a terminal that stopped reading, longer only while a just-opened port settles). The watchdog is fed while it waits. Then a system reset (AIRCR SYSRESETREQ). Core.ST.L4: if the chip still believes its flash is empty (it was flashed blank by DFU or SWD and not power-cycled since), that stale verdict is corrected first, so the reset starts this program and not the ROM bootloader. Core.ST.H5 with BOOT0 held high resets into the ROM bootloader. Safe from an interrupt handler; the BLE disconnect is then left to the central's supervision timeout.

functions.name: core_reset_reason
functions.brief: Why the Core last reset: power-on (or brownout), the reset pin, the watchdog, a software reset (core_reset(), a remote reset from Studio, an update), or other. Read once by core_init() and kept, so it answers the same for the whole run.
functions.return_desc: core_reset_reason_t: 0 power-on, 1 pin, 2 watchdog, 3 software, 4 other.

functions.name: core_st_reset_flags
functions.brief: The raw STM32 RCC reset flags read at boot (CORE_ST_RESET_FLAG_*; bits 31..24). 0 if no flag was set. ST silicon only: portable code uses core_reset_reason().

functions.name: core_reset_capture
functions.brief: Read and keep the reset flags, then clear them in RCC. core_init() calls this first thing; later calls do nothing. core_reset_reason() calls it too, for a program that never ran core_init().

functions.name: ll_pwr_enable_backup_access
functions.brief: Enable access to the backup domain (RTC, backup registers). Must be called before writing to RTC or backup registers.

functions.name: ll_pwr_sleep_wfi
functions.brief: Enter Sleep mode. CPU clock stopped, all peripherals continue running. Wakes on any enabled interrupt. Use WFI (wait for interrupt) or WFE (wait for event).

functions.name: ll_pwr_stop
functions.brief: Enter Stop mode (lowest power with SRAM retention). All oscillators stopped except LSI/LSE. Wakes via EXTI (GPIO, RTC alarm, etc.). After waking, clock is MSI/HSI — you must reinitialize the PLL if needed. On L4: Stop 0, Stop 1, or Stop 2 available. On WBA/H5: Stop 0 or Stop 1.

functions.name: ll_pwr_standby
functions.brief: Enter Standby mode (lowest power, SRAM lost). Only RTC, IWDG, and wakeup pins remain powered. On wake, the MCU resets (starts from Reset_Handler). WARNING: All SRAM contents are lost. Save state to backup registers or flash before entering standby.

functions.name: ll_pwr_woke_from_standby
functions.brief: Check if we woke from standby. The flag is not cleared by a system reset, so it stays set across later resets until ll_pwr_clear_standby_flag().

functions.name: ll_pwr_clear_standby_flag
functions.brief: Clear the standby flag

types.name: core_reset_reason_t
types.brief: Cause of the reset this program started from (core_reset_reason()).

members.name: CORE_RESET_POWER_ON
members.description: Power-on, or a brownout (one flag for both)

members.name: CORE_RESET_PIN
members.description: NRST pin: a reset button or a debug probe

members.name: CORE_RESET_SOFTWARE
members.description: core_reset(), a remote reset, the DFU touch, an update's restart, SWD

members.name: CORE_RESET_OTHER
members.description: Illegal low-power entry, firewall, or no flag
